propositions: Jira Data Center rate-limiting (introduced in 8.6, DC-only, admin-configurable token-bucket) is not honoured by rebar; 429 responses propagate as hard failures on first occurrence instead of triggering retry
Retry-After header present in 429 responses must be parsed and honoured with up to 20% random jitter and 60-second clamp, reusing existing `_errors.parse_retry_after` and `MAX_BACKOFF_S`

429 retry must be scoped to idempotent reads only via per-call opt-in defaulting to OFF, because `_with_connection_retry` is the single choke point for all 15 transport call sites including mutations, and a 429 can arrive after the server began a write
Exhausted 429 retry cap must raise `BackendHTTPError(code=429)` through the adapter boundary, never a raw `JIRAError`, to maintain the boundary contract that callers catch `BackendHTTPError`

Implementation requires extracting the retry/error cluster from transport.py (at 789/800 line cap with only 11 lines headroom) into a new module `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` to make room for policy logic
The duplicate-issue class (rebar:21fc) risk exists because nothing in a 429 response distinguishes whether it arrived before or after the server began processing a write
